candidates.attacker_control: HTTP request parameters (URI query, POST body, multipart fields) are captured in Dispatcher.createContextMap (Dispatcher.java:664-686: ActionContext.PARAMETERS and the OGNL 'parameters' key) and injected onto the value stack as action properties by ParametersInterceptor.setParameters (ParametersInterceptor.java:210-214). An application or template that places such a value inside a %{...}/${...}-evaluated attribute or result parameter (the framework's documented altSyntax usage; examples in this repo: rest-showcase orders-edit.jsp:51 '%%{#request.contextPath}/orders/%%{id}', showcase edit-person.jsp:54-61 'name="persons(%%{id}).name" value="%%{name}"', custom template mytemplate.jsp:26 '%%{parameters.paramName}') thereby supplies attacker-chosen OGNL text to the evaluator.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Verified in source: (a) OgnlTextParser has a loop-counter guard (lines 39-48) that blocks naive re-evaluation of a value substituted into the same '%' pass, and 'pos' is declared before the open-char loop (line 32) and carried over, so the obvious mixed '$'->'%' two-pass re-evaluation did not survive inspection; I therefore do not claim a verified runtime second evaluation. (b) Request parameters are not evaluated automatically - exploitation requires the app to interpolate request-derived text into a %{}/$ {} attribute/result value. (c) The default sandbox blocks major gadget classes/packages and static method access. (d) No test or runtime artifacts exist in the snapshot (src/main only), so exploitability was not confirmed.
candidates.impact: Arbitrary OGNL expression evaluation in the application's value-stack context (read request/session/application data, invoke sandbox-allowed methods, mutate context values). With a sandbox escape this becomes remote code execution, matching the vendor severity for this release line; without one it is still an expression-injection/defense-in-depth failure with confidentiality and integrity impact.
candidates.prerequisites: 1) Target app uses altSyntax %{...} tag attributes (default: struts.tag.altSyntax=true) or ${...} result/localized-text values and interpolates request-derived data into them; 2) for code execution, an OGNL sandbox bypass is needed (SecurityMemberAccess + struts-default.xml excludedClasses/excludedPackageNames block Runtime, ProcessBuilder, Class, java.io/net/nio, javax.*, xwork internals; struts.ognl.allowStaticMethodAccess=false by default). The vendor rates the equivalent 2.5.25 flaw as critical RCE, but the bypass itself is not demonstrated in this source review.
candidates.root_cause: The expression-translation layer does not distinguish trusted literal text from request-derived text. Component.findValue(String, Class) (Component.java:371-383) treats any String containing '%{' and '}' as an OGNL template and calls TextParseUtil.translateVariables('%', expr, stack); ComponentUtils.containsExpression (ComponentUtils.java:64-70) checks only for the substrings. TextParseUtil.translateVariables (TextParseUtil.java:155-170) hands each %{...} body to stack.findValue(parsedValue, asType), i.e. arbitrary OGNL, and OgnlTextParser.evaluate (OgnlTextParser.java:28-100) replaces the matched region with the resolved value and keeps scanning the mutated string (lines 64-96), the only restriction being a per-open-char loop counter (lines 39-48, default 1 in TextParser.java:27). altSyntax is on by default (default.properties:124-126), so this applies to every UI/body tag (UIBean.evaluateParams, UIBean.java:637-760; StrutsBodyTagSupport.findValue, StrutsBodyTagSupport.java:43-62; dynamic attributes, AbstractUITag.java:304-310) and to result locations/headers via the two-open-char translateVariables (StrutsResultSupport.conditionalParse, StrutsResultSupport.java:204-249; HttpHeaderResult.java:182-205).
candidates.title: Forced OGNL evaluation of user-influenced tag-attribute / result values in Struts 2.5.25 (%{} altSyntax, S2-061 / CVE-2020-17530 class)
candidates.trace: Request parameter -> Dispatcher.createContextMap (Dispatcher.java:671,685) / ParametersInterceptor (lines 210-214) -> value stack -> JSP tag attribute containing %{...} (e.g. ComponentTagSupport.populateParams -> UIBean.evaluateParams, UIBean.java:637-760) -> Component.findString/findValue (Component.java:219-220, 371-383) -> ComponentUtils.containsExpression (ComponentUtils.java:68-70) -> TextParseUtil.translateVariables('%', expr, stack) (TextParseUtil.java:84-86,155-170) -> OgnlTextParser.evaluate parses each %{...} body and calls evaluator -> stack.findValue(parsedValue, asType) (TextParseUtil.java:157-164) -> OGNL execution through SecurityMemberAccess. Result/header configs follow the same path with openChars {'$','%'} (TextParseUtil.java:47-49) via StrutsResultSupport.conditionalParse (lines 216-225) and HttpHeaderResult (line 185).
candidates.unverified: No runtime confirmation and no complete exploit chain: the exact OGNL sandbox-escape primitive for 2.5.25, whether a specific bundled application is exploitable end-to-end, and whether the upstream 2.5.26 fix changed these exact lines (offline review cannot diff against the fixed release). The claim that this is the case's canonical CVE is an inference from the version tag, not proven.
candidates.weakness_type: OGNL expression injection (CWE-917), forced/double evaluation leading to potential RCE

coverage_summary: Reviewed the core OGNL/tag/result pipeline (Component, UIBean, AbstractUITag, StrutsBodyTagSupport, TextParseUtil, OgnlTextParser, ComponentUtils, SecurityMemberAccess, OgnlUtil, ParametersInterceptor, dispatcher/context creation, StrutsResultSupport, HttpHeaderResult, redirect/stream/action-redirect results), the default security configuration (struts-default.xml excluded classes/packages, default.properties), and sampled app JSPs/templates in apps/showcase and apps/rest-showcase for interpolation patterns. Used the P1 index only for navigation (symbols/facts/edges) and verified every cited element against source text. P1 scope states: 1,824 source files, 1,730 indexed, 94 omitted from the index; relations are syntax-level candidates only, with no control-flow/data-flow/semantic analysis and no runtime reachability. Areas not reviewed in depth: embeddedjsp Jasper fork, OSGi/Spring/CDI/DWR/Tiles/portlet plugins, sitegraph, jasperreports/jfreechart plugins, most showcase chat/hangman/ajax/validation templates.
limitations: Static, source-only review: no build, tests, scanners, or runtime execution were performed; exploitability and sandbox escape are not confirmed.
The P1 relation index omits 94 files and provides only syntactic call/containment/inheritance candidates; no data-flow or reachability proof is available.
The snapshot contains src/main only (no tests), so upstream security tests that would demonstrate the flaw are unavailable.
Attribution to CVE-2020-17530 / S2-061 is inferred from the 2.5.25 version tag and the affected version ranges; the upstream fixed code could not be diffed offline.
Grep-based coverage cannot guarantee that no other single-file issue exists in the uninspected plugins/apps listed in the coverage summary.

rejected_leads.lead: apps/showcase JSPEvalAction writes attacker-controlled JSP (request parameter 'jsp') into an exploded-WAR file (/interactive/demo.jsp) and the @After hook only truncates it afterwards (JSPEvalAction.java:35-63, mapped in struts-interactive.xml:33-38).
rejected_leads.reason: Demo/teaching action in the showcase WAR, requires an exploded deployment and a race between rendering and cleanup; it is an application-level dangerous pattern rather than a core framework vulnerability and is not the version-specific flaw.

rejected_leads.lead: Mixed '$'/'%' two-open-char double evaluation in StrutsResultSupport.conditionalParse / HttpHeaderResult (TextParseUtil.java:47-49,155-170; OgnlTextParser.java:28-100).
rejected_leads.reason: On inspection the parser shares one 'pos' across open-char passes (OgnlTextParser.java:32,90-93), so a value substituted by the '$' pass is positioned before 'pos' and is not re-scanned by the '%' pass at maxLoopCount=1; not verified exploitable, so not submitted separately.
Uses NoTypePermission.NONE plus per-action/default explicit permissions; appears to be the S2-052 fix and no bypass was identified.

rejected_leads.lead: DefaultStaticContentLoader static resource serving (/struts/*, /static/*) with URLDecoder in buildPath (DefaultStaticContentLoader.java:196-310).
rejected_leads.reason: Lookups are restricted to configured package prefixes and the resolved URL must end with the expected path; no concrete traversal/read primitive established.

rejected_leads.lead: config-browser ListValidatorsAction loads an arbitrary class name from the request via ClassLoaderUtil.loadClass (plugins/config-browser/.../ListValidatorsAction.java:95-109).
rejected_leads.reason: Dev/diagnostic plugin that must be explicitly deployed; class loading alone (no instantiation of the named class, only validator metadata lookup) has limited impact and is not the snapshot's release-specific vulnerability.

summary: Snapshot is Apache Struts 2.5.25 (pom.xml:32, SCM tag STRUTS_2_5_25) — the last release affected by the forced-OGNL-evaluation class of issues (fixed in 2.5.26 / S2-061, CVE-2020-17530). The strongest source-grounded issue is that tag-attribute / result values containing %{...} (or ${...}) are executed as OGNL against the value stack, with no trust distinction for text that originated from the HTTP request. Component.findValue(String,Class) routes any string containing "%{" + "}" into TextParseUtil.translateVariables('%',...), which passes the raw body to ValueStack.findValue(...); OgnlTextParser splices resolved values back into the scanned string and continues, with only a per-open-char maxLoopCount guard. Because Dispatcher puts all request parameters into the ActionContext ("#parameters") and ParametersInterceptor writes them onto the stack as action properties, an application/template that interpolates request-derived data inside a %{}/$ {} attribute (a documented pattern that appears in the bundled apps) turns attacker text into OGNL. Impact ranges from expression-level data access to remote code execution via sandbox escape; the vendor classifies this version's flaw as critical RCE.
